content:
Rado Kirov said:

That's not how Reservoir works, it adds projects automatically; see https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/inclusion-criteria

Ah apologies, that makes sense. I wonder if the maintainers are interested in evolving it to support more features like formalization.yaml (getting off-topic for the original thread)

This is an intriguing idea! What would we like Reservoir to do with a formalization.yaml? Just display some check mark advertising that it exists? Even that seems like a wonderful start.

@Johan Commelin, @Mac Malone, shall we?

One of the plans we had as part of the formal frontier project is to create some sort of dashboard for projects with formalization.yaml. If this can become part of reservoir that would be even better! Ping @Bhavik Mehta

Related to this, I have a site with stats from Reservoir. I recently added the formalization.yaml as one of the included items. For example:

  • all packages with a formalization.yaml
  • the contents of the formalization.yaml rendered for a specific repo

The main point of the site is to understand the dependency graph of the packages on Reservoir, but out of curiosity I added the formalization.yaml and Palomar status.

How will "we track projects with a formalization.yaml" and "we track Palomar projects" differ in the medium-term? Is the latter also meant to pick up "we're building theory, but without a main statement as goal" projects?
